# 2 Baruch Chapter 28 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**28:1** And-he-answered and-said to-me: Whatever-will-be-then will-have-in-it the-seal-of-that-time; [it] will-last twelve years.

**28:2** And-I-said to-him: But-is-it-good-for-a-man to-live-then?

**28:3** And-he-answered and-said to-me: Ask-me not-concerning that.

**28:4** For those-who-will-be-living then — they-will-not-perceive any-distress, for-they-will-know-not that-it-is-the-end-of-the-times.

**28:5** And-those-who-are-righteous-and-wise-in-that-time — they-will-not-perceive [the] tribulations, for-they-will-go-forth out-of-this-world.

**28:6** And-the-many-who-are-not-wise — those-will-be-in-great-distress.

**28:7** And-it-will-come-to-pass after-all-these-things that-when-the-time-of-the-appointed-[end]-is-fulfilled, the-Anointed-One will-begin to-be-revealed.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. The revelation of the Messiah (v.7) comes immediately after the twelve woes are completed. "Anointed One" renders Syriac meshicha (= Hebrew mashiach). The wise are exempt from perceiving the tribulation — a doctrine of righteous preservation.*
